facts.fact: The vendor recommends that a business's monthly digital spend be at least $1,500-$2,000 before adding TV.
facts.quote: Your monthly digital spend is at least $1,500-$2,000.

facts.fact: The vendor says local service businesses with strong word-of-mouth may layer TV on top of as little as $800/month in digital spend.
facts.quote: where even $800/month in digital plus TV can layer well because the trust building has another reinforcement loop.

facts.fact: The vendor claims direct attribution captures only 30-50% of TV's real lift.
facts.quote: because direct attribution captures only 30-50% of TV's real lift.

facts.fact: The vendor recommends running a TV test with the rest of the digital plan held steady for a 60-90 day window.
facts.quote: Plan for a 60-90 day window with TV layered in and the rest of your plan steady.

facts.fact: The vendor recommends a Tier 1 TV starting budget of $800-$1,200 per month for businesses with $500-$1,500 in total monthly digital spend.
facts.quote: Start TV at $800-$1,200/month.

facts.fact: The vendor's Tier 1 tier covers businesses with $500-$1,500 in total monthly digital spend.
facts.quote: **Tier 1: $500-$1,500 total monthly digital, adding TV.**

facts.fact: The vendor recommends a Tier 2 TV starting budget of $1,500-$2,500 per month for businesses with $2,000-$5,000 in total monthly digital spend.
facts.quote: Start TV at $1,500-$2,500/month.

facts.fact: The vendor states that a Tier 2 test with $2,000-$5,000 in monthly digital spend produces a defensible read in 60-75 days.
facts.quote: the test produces a defensible read in 60-75 days.

facts.fact: The vendor recommends a Tier 3 TV starting budget of $2,500-$5,000 per month for businesses with more than $5,000 in total monthly digital spend.
facts.quote: Start TV at $2,500-$5,000/month.

facts.fact: The vendor says businesses with $5,000+ in total monthly digital spend may test TV in two geographic areas, one with TV and one without.
facts.quote: **Tier 3: $5,000+ total monthly digital, adding TV.**

facts.fact: The vendor says that if a business uses an agency for TV creative, it should budget $2,000-$8,000 for initial production.
facts.quote: If you're producing through an agency, budget $2,000-$8,000 for initial production.

facts.fact: The vendor recommends capturing 4 weeks of pre-TV performance data as a baseline before TV launches.
facts.quote: Capture 4 weeks of pre-TV performance.

facts.fact: The vendor states that a Google search ad must deliver its message within 90 characters.
facts.quote: the search ad has to deliver in 90 characters.

facts.fact: Vendor states that a baseline approach captures 70-90% of TV's true contribution for most small businesses, compared with 30-50% from direct attribution alone.
facts.quote: For most small businesses, this baseline approach captures 70-90% of TV's true contribution, compared to 30-50% with direct attribution alone.

facts.fact: Vendor says TV needs 2-3 weeks to settle and another 4-6 weeks to show its lift on the rest of the funnel, so judgments should wait 60-90 days.
facts.quote: TV needs 2-3 weeks to settle and another 4-6 weeks to demonstrate its lift on the rest of your funnel. Two-week judgments produce false negatives. Plan for 60-90 days.

facts.fact: Vendor says even good TV creative degrades after 8-10 weeks and recommends refreshing creative at the 8-week mark.
facts.quote: Even great creative degrades after 8-10 weeks. Plan to refresh creative at the 8-week mark, or sooner if your conversion data is declining.

facts.fact: Vendor suggests that after strong cross-channel lift with healthy direct attribution (total inquiries up 20%+), TV should be scaled by 25-50%.
facts.quote: Total inquiries up 20%+ over baseline, Meta and Google metrics improving, branded search and direct traffic up. The right move is usually to scale TV by 25-50%

facts.fact: Vendor states that a 5-10% inquiry lift on a $1,500 TV spend is often profitable on booked-revenue math for local home services.
facts.quote: For local home services, 5-10% lift on a $1,500 TV spend is often profitable on the booked-revenue math.

facts.fact: Vendor recommends a starting TV test budget of $800-$2,500 per month, depending on total existing digital spend.
facts.quote: Start at $800-$2,500/month depending on your total existing digital spend.

facts.fact: Vendor lists a readiness signal that monthly digital spend should be at least $1,500-$2,000 before adding TV.
facts.quote: your monthly digital spend is at least $1,500-$2,000

facts.fact: Vendor says a TV test budget should produce local frequency of 3-5 impressions per household over the campaign window.
facts.quote: large enough to produce meaningful local frequency (3-5 impressions per household over the campaign window)

facts.fact: Vendor lists frequency under 2 as a common cause of no measurable TV lift, meaning the audience never saw the ad enough times.
facts.quote: frequency under 2 (audience never saw the ad enough times)

facts.fact: Vendor says self-serving through a platform like Adwave suits most small businesses with monthly digital spend under $10,000, while agencies make more sense above $20,000+ per month.
facts.quote: For most small businesses with monthly digital spend under $10,000, self-serving through a platform like Adwave produces strong results

facts.fact: Vendor says cross-channel lift signals often begin emerging in weeks 3-4 after TV launches, while the most defensible read requires a 60-90 day pre/post comparison.
facts.quote: Cross-channel lift signals (branded search, direct traffic, Meta and Google metric improvements) often start emerging in weeks 3-4

facts.fact: Vendor's framework says the first serious cross-channel comparison happens in weeks 5-6, comparing weeks 1-6 against weeks -4 to -1.
facts.quote: Week 5-6. First serious cross-channel comparison. Pull total inquiries (or whatever your primary metric is) for weeks 1-6 vs. The same metric for weeks -4 to -1.

facts.fact: Vendor's pattern for modest lift (total inquiries up 5-10%, Meta and Google roughly steady) says to consider testing different creative for another 60 days before deciding.
facts.quote: Consider testing different creative for another 60 days before deciding.
